summary:
Our project aims to develop a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) methodology using QGIS to identify areas on Earth with geological and surface characteristics similar to those found on Mars and the Moon. We selected the El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve in Sonora, Mexico, because of its lava fields, volcanic craters, and arid landscapes.

The project addresses this challenge by analyzing geological, topographic, and geomorphological data, as well as satellite images and digital elevation models. This information will help us identify and classify areas according to their surface conditions, slopes, and potential obstacles, in order to determine which locations may be suitable for controlled tests related to future space missions.

This project is important because it allows us to study planetary-like environments on Earth, improve landing-site assessment methods, and support the development of technologies for future space exploration.
details:
Our project uses Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to identify areas on Earth with geological and surface conditions similar to those of Mars and the Moon. We selected the El Pinacate and Gran Desierto de Altar Biosphere Reserve in Sonora, Mexico, as our study area.

The project works by analyzing geological maps, satellite images, topography, elevation models, terrain slopes, and surface characteristics through QGIS. These layers are combined to identify areas with favorable conditions for controlled landing-related tests.

Its main benefits include improving the understanding of planetary environments, identifying potential landing zones, and supporting future space exploration research. The expected impact is to provide a useful geospatial method for studying Earth locations that can serve as analog environments for Mars and the Moon.

The main tools include QGIS, Google Earth, satellite imagery, digital elevation models, and geological data from sources such as NASA, USGS, and INEGI. No specific programming language or specialized hardware was required during the preliminary stage.

The creative aspect of the project is applying civil engineering and geographic analysis to a space exploration challenge. Our team considered geological similarities, terrain conditions, slope, surface obstacles, accessibility, and environmental protection when selecting and evaluating the study area.
